children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures remained weaker on Monday, despite losses in comparable oils improving.
Crude oil was sharply higher following the exchange of attacks between the United States and Iran in the Middle East.

The spillover from crude saw the Chicago soy complex overcome earlier losses in soybeans and soyoil for their nearby contracts to close relatively steady, but soymeal remained lower on the day. European rapeseed also softened its declines, while Malaysian palm oil was closed for a holiday.
An analyst said profit-taking and pressure from the impending canola harvest likely weighed on canola values as well.

Over the next few days Prairie temperatures are to be in the low to mid 20s degrees Celsius. That should help with the region's harvest, although much of Saskatchewan and parts of western Manitoba got rain on Monday.
Despite canola losing ground its November contract held above its major moving averages.
The Canadian dollar was stronger on Monday afternoon, with the loonie rising to 72.17 U.S. cents, compared to Friday's close of 72.00.
There were 57,306 canola contracts traded on Monday, compared to 68,101 on Friday. Spreading accounted for 30,380 contracts traded.
